goal: A step session lands its own pull request. It writes `done` and `pr` into its step, commits that with the code, opens the pull request and runs `mc merge <repo> <pr>` itself; a red gate comes back to the same session, which fixes it with the diff already in its context and runs `mc merge` again on the same pull request; a green gate is the merge, and nothing measures that tree a second time. There is no repair session, no `held.json`, no merge lane and no second round: the gate runs once per green, and a pull request a session could not land is a person's through the brief, with nothing in between (ruling 21, Martin 2026-09-12: "Det borde inte finnas något utrymmet för en 'repair'"; "runner step kör direkt 'mc merge #'. Då körs direkt rätt tester. Om fel, fås svaret tillbaka och kan fixas. Om grönt, så sker merge direkt och inga tester behöver köras ytterligare en gång.").

Measured 2026-09-05..12 over 235 step and repair sessions in `~/mc/runner/log/runs.tsv`: 184 landed; 21 were `success,open,gate-red` or another gate stop, each costing a fresh repair session that re-read everything (22 repair rows, 156 minutes, median 33 turns) and a second gate round on the same pull request; the gate's red names reached that session through `held.json` and `repairPrompt`, never the session that wrote the code. The step role (`canon/roles/step.md` line 28) says "Do not merge: the runner lands it after you", and the prompt (`stepPrompt`, `src/mc/run-plan.js` line 793) ends "Do not merge. Do not ask questions. Stop when the PR exists." — so the session that could fix a red in a few turns is gone before the gate speaks.

`mc merge` today refuses rather than waits: the gate lock (`takeGateLock`, `src/mc/gate-lock.js`) answers `busy` and the lease (`claimLease` in `runMergeRound`, `src/mc/repo-merge.js` line 163) answers `lease`, and the verb then writes the pull request into `~/mc/runner/merges.json` for the runner's merge lane (`queueRefusal`, `src/mc/commands/repo.js` line 300) and exits 0. The waiting is the runner's, in `landPr` (`src/mc/run.js` line 697, `BUSY_STOPS`, `LAND_RETRY_MS` 30 s, `LAND_WAIT_MS`). With two lanes whose sessions both end in `mc merge`, the waiting has to be the verb's, in order of arrival, and the next waiter takes the gate the moment the round before it releases it.
contract: `mc merge <repo> <pr>` stays the one door (Martin, 2026-09-02: only `mc merge` may be used). Its measurement — `runGate`, the lease across the round, the base re-check, the squash, `tree_identical` — does not change; only who calls it, and what it does while another round holds the machine.

A step session's `done` and `pr` are in the pull request, in the same commit as the code: `mc merge` lands both or neither, and a red gate leaves `main` untouched. A step is never set `done` by the runner, and a plan on `main` is never written by anything but a landed pull request.

The step session sets its step `done` before it opens the pull request, as today; what it does after that is `mc merge`, on that pull request and no other, until it is merged or the session gives up. A session that gives up sets nothing in the plan and says why in the pull request: an open pull request on a project branch is a person's, through the brief.

The plan boundary (`unauthorisedChanges`, `src/mc/plan-schema.js` line 395) is checked at the door, by `mc merge`, before the gate runs — a session cannot land a plan trespass by landing its own pull request. What a step session may write in its plan does not change.

There is no repair session, of any kind: not per project, not from a merge lane. A pull request the gate refused and its session did not fix stays open, and the runner starts nothing on it. What the gate saw reaches the person through the pull request's own comments and `gate-rounds.jsonl`, not through a runner file.

`runs.tsv` keeps every column it has, in order. `kind` never reads `repair` for a row written after step 3 lands; `note` says `success,merged` when the session's own `mc merge` landed the branch's pull request, `success,open` when it left one open, and `success` when there is none.

A `mc merge` that waits returns within the Bash ceiling a session has (`BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS: '600000'`, `src/mc/run.js` line 246): it waits at most `MERGE_WAIT_MS` (8 minutes) for its turn, then says so and exits without losing its place — the caller runs it again.
out_of_scope: The gate subtracting tests already red on `main` from a candidate's red. Raised by Martin the same day and real (`mc-merge.md` § *Red, and since when* knows the streak; the merge round does not read it), but a gate change of its own, planned separately.

Step-cost step 3 (the check-in message and the stall kill, `docs/project/mc/step-cost/PLAN.json`), and any change to how a session is spawned. This project changes what the session is told to do at the end and what `mc merge` does when called, not the session's lifetime.

Memoro: its `AGENTS.md`, its test selection, its command gates, its plans. Which tests a memoro step runs before its pull request is memoro's; this project makes the session run the gate, which is the same selection the merge runs.

`mc merge --docs` (`src/mc/docs-merge.js`) and the runner's own docs landings (`landDocsPr`: the archive pull request and the block pull request). They land nothing a session wrote and keep their door.

Batches (`mc merge <repo> <pr> <pr>`), stacks (`stackOrder`, `replayOnto`, `landProject` for more than one pull request) and `mc test`. A step session opens one pull request from the branch it stands on; a stack is a session that could not branch from main, which `freshBranch` already prevents, and it is not planned here beyond leaving the code as it is.
The brief's proposals for a held pull request beyond renaming the section: what a person does with an open, unlanded pull request (merge by hand, close, block) is `mc brief`'s and stays.

steps.title: `mc merge` waits for its turn, in order of arrival, and refuses a plan trespass at the door
comments: Built as specified: waitTurn() in src/mc/commands/repo.js owns the whole wait — the merges.json entry, the one-time "waiting behind" line, the "waited Ns" line, the MERGE_WAIT_MS timeout line and its exit 3, all in one function, called from gate()'s single-PR loop with a contended flag so a round that just reported busy/lease is forced through the full wait rather than re-reading a lock that already looks free. nextWaiter() in merge-queue.js takes the oldest live entry, across every repository, deferring to a waiter whose own repository lease is held. busy and lease are removed from QUEUEABLE_STOPS. The door is planBoundary() in the new src/mc/merge-boundary.js: gh pr view for the branch, projectForBranch to find the project (or skip the check entirely), unauthorisedChanges(mainPlan, headPlan, stepOfPr(...)) to find a trespass, fail-open on any gh/git/no-project-match failure, fail-closed only for a genuine trespass or an unparseable head plan.

Found and fixed a real bug along the way, not anticipated going in: merge-queue.js normalise() computed pid as Number.isFinite(Number(entry.pid)) ? Number(entry.pid) : null — but Number(null) is 0, a finite number, so a refusal-queue entry (pid: null, not a waiter) written to merges.json and read back a second time silently became pid: 0, which dropDeadEntries/nextWaiter would then treat as a live waiter with pid 0. Fixed by checking entry.pid == null first; regression test added to merge-queue.test.js covering the exact JSON round-trip.

Scoped to a single mc merge <repo> <pr>: the door does not run for a batch (mc merge <repo> <pr1> <pr2>), so a batch pull request from a project branch is not checked against its plan by this step. Said plainly in docs/technical/mc-merge.md § The door as a known gap, not hidden. Extending the door to batches, and the wait queue to more than the single-PR path, is out of this step’s instruction and left for whoever picks it up.

success_criteria[0] and [1] are left met: false. Both are verified against their check: (—the fake-lock/fake-lease wait behaviour, the ordering, the timeout, and each plan-trespass fixture all pass in tests/mc/merge-command.test.js and tests/mc/merge-boundary.test.js. But each criterion also has a Live: clause (no stopped_at: "busy" end line in gate-rounds.jsonl after a runner session's mc merge; a real stopped_at: "plan-trespass" round logged) that only a live runner round after this lands can produce — not something this session can produce or observe. Marking met: true on a live claim this session never measured would say something it does not know.

The MERGES page label changed from "queued" to "waiting" in src/mc/page-render.js (mergesLines): merges.json now holds both refusal-queue entries and this step's own live waiters, and the earlier label read as though nothing there was actually waiting on anything. tests/mc/page.test.js updated to match.

docs/technical/mc-merge.md § One round at a time rewritten for the wait, plus a new § The door; docs/technical/mc-run.md's § A hand mc merge that was refused becomes the runner's had its first paragraph rewritten to say busy/lease no longer queue there. changelog.d/mc-merge-waits-and-checks-the-plan-door.md added.

While finishing this step, origin/main gained #710 (ruling 21, the register: step state now lives in ~/mc/runner/projects/<project>.json, with the file's own status/pr/comments/blocked_by kept for backward compatibility per docs/project/README.md). canon/roles/step.md, which is this session's own contract, was not touched by that commit, so this PR still writes steps[0] directly and lets the merge carry the diff, as instructed. Merged origin/main into this branch cleanly (auto-merge, no conflicts) before finishing; npm test is green at 1982 tests, 1973 pass, 0 fail, 9 skipped, after the merge.
steps.done_when: `mc merge <repo> <pr>` against a held gate lock or lease waits in `merges.json` order, up to `MERGE_WAIT_MS`, and runs the round when it is the oldest live waiter and both are free; past the limit it prints one `run this again` line, keeps its entry and exits 3; a pull request from a project branch whose `PLAN.json` changed outside its step's writable fields stops at `plan-trespass` before the gate, with every problem printed; `docs/technical/mc-merge.md` describes both; the suite is green.
instruction: Read first: `gate()` and `queueRefusal()` in `src/mc/commands/repo.js` (lines 300–386 — the verb runs `runMergeRound`, records the round, and on a queueable stop writes `merges.json` and exits 0); `takeGateLock`, `runningRound`, `describeRunning` in `src/mc/gate-lock.js` (one file, one pid, no expiry, a dead pid is reaped by the next claim); `claimLease` at `src/mc/repo-merge.js` line 163 and the `lease` stop it returns; `src/mc/merge-queue.js` whole (`enqueue`, `dequeue`, `queueOrder` oldest-first by `since`, `QUEUEABLE_STOPS`); `landPr` in `src/mc/run.js` lines 674–733, which is the wait this step moves into the verb (`BUSY_STOPS = ['busy', 'lease']`, `LAND_RETRY_MS` 30 s); `unauthorisedChanges` and `readPlanText` in `src/mc/plan-schema.js`; `stepOfPr` in `src/mc/run-plan.js` line 297; `projectForBranch` in `src/mc/project-prs.js` line 34; the post-session trespass check in `src/mc/run.js` lines 2037–2054, which is the check this step puts at the door. Tests: `tests/mc/merge-command.test.js`, `tests/mc/gate-lock.test.js`, `tests/mc/repo-merge-live.test.js`.

The wait. In `gate()`, before `runMergeRound` and only when `mode` is `merge` (a `--check` measures and may still be refused as today): write this call into `merges.json` as a waiter — `enqueue` with `repo`, `pr`, `branch` (from `gh pr view <pr> --json headRefName`, asked once), `since`, `holder`, and a new `pid: process.pid` — then loop: read `runningRound()` and `readLease(repoPath)`; drop every entry whose `pid` is not alive (the same `isAlive` gate-lock.js uses, exported or duplicated in one line); if the oldest remaining entry for this repository is this process and neither lock nor lease is held, dequeue self and run the round; otherwise sleep `MERGE_POLL_MS` (15 s) and try again. Print one `mc: waiting behind <describeRunning(running) or the lease's holder and errand> — <n> ahead of this one` line on stderr the first time it waits and one `mc: waited <s>s` line when it stops waiting. Past `MERGE_WAIT_MS` (8 minutes, a constant beside `LAND_RETRY_MS`'s old home with the reason: a session's Bash call is capped at ten minutes, `BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` in run.js) print `mc: still waiting behind … after 8 min — run this again; the place in the queue is kept` and exit 3, leaving the entry. A second `mc merge` for the same repository and pull request from a new pid replaces the entry's `pid` and keeps its `since` (`enqueue` already keeps `since`). The runner's own `landPr` keeps its loop for now — step 2 removes its callers and step 3 the function — so nothing in run.js changes in this step.

Order of arrival is the file, not the lock: the oldest live entry is the one allowed to take the lock, so a round that has just released the gate is followed by the waiter that arrived first, not by whichever process polled first. Two waiters on different repositories are both bounded by the one gate lock and each by its own lease, so the rule is `oldest live entry across all repositories takes the lock; a waiter behind a lease it cannot get keeps its place`. Say this in a comment on the loop.

What `merges.json` is afterwards. Today it is what a refused round handed the runner's merge lane; after this step it is the waiters, and the page's MERGES section (`src/mc/merges-collect.js`, `page-render.js` line 659) reads it as the queue — the same rows with `pid` added, so the section needs no change here beyond the label saying `waiting` where it said `queued`. Keep `queueRefusal` for the `red`, `pr-tests`, `extra-gate` and `merge` stops in this step exactly as it is — the lane that reads them is step 3's to remove, and a step landing in between must not leave a refused hand merge in no file at all. Remove `busy` and `lease` from `QUEUEABLE_STOPS`: a round that waited cannot stop there any more, and `queueable('busy')` returning true would enqueue a second entry for a process that is already a waiter.

The door. Before the wait and before the gate: ask GitHub for the pull request's `headRefName` and `baseRefName` (one `gh pr view --json`), and if `projectForBranch(headRefName, <names>)` names a project — `names` being every `docs/project/*/*/PLAN.json` on `origin/<base>` after a fetch, read the way `plansOnMain` reads them in run.js — read that project's `PLAN.json` at `origin/<base>` (`git show origin/main:<path>`) and at the pull request's head (`git show origin/<headRefName>:<path>`; fetch first). If the head's copy does not parse, stop at `plan-trespass` with `the plan no longer parses: <first problem>`. Otherwise `unauthorisedChanges(mainPlan, headPlan, stepOfPr(headPlan, pr))`; not ok is `finish('plan-trespass', problems.join('; '))`, printed one problem per line as `mc: plan-trespass — <problem>`, recorded in `gate-rounds.jsonl` like any stop, never queued, exit 1. A head whose plan is byte-identical to main's passes without the comparison (a docs-only or code-only pull request from a project branch). A branch that is no project's is not checked: a planning session's `plan/<programme>` branch rewrites plans on purpose. Put the check in a function of its own (`planBoundary({ repoPath, pr, git, gh })` in a new `src/mc/merge-boundary.js`, pure over the two texts and the index where it can be), because step 2 makes the runner rely on it and step 3 deletes the runner's own copy.

The index. `stepOfPr(headPlan, pr)` is the step naming this pull request, or the deliverable step when none does yet — the same rule `repairBaseline` uses in run.js. A session that forgot to write `pr` is judged against its deliverable step, which is right; a session that wrote another step's `pr` is a trespass on that step, which is also right.

Tests. Extend `tests/mc/merge-command.test.js` (the `gate` function takes `deps` — `mergeRound`, `read`, `readRunner`, `alive`, `now`, `writeJson` are already injectable; add `sleep`, `runningRound`, `readLease`, `git`, `gh` the same way) for: a free machine runs the round at once and writes no entry; a held lock with a live pid makes the verb wait, and it runs the round after the fake lock is released; two waiters started in order run in that order; a waiter past `MERGE_WAIT_MS` exits 3 with its entry kept; a dead pid's entry is dropped by the next waiter; `plan-trespass` for a head that edits another step's `instruction`, for one that edits `goal`, and for a head whose plan does not parse; no trespass for a head that changes only `status`, `pr`, `comments`, `blocked_by` and `met`; no check for a `plan/mc` branch. `merge-queue.test.js` (if it exists; else beside it): `queueable('busy')` is false. Run `npm test` once at the end, in the foreground.

Docs. `docs/technical/mc-merge.md` § *One round at a time* (line 419): the two leases still refuse a second round, and `mc merge` now waits on both in `merges.json` order, up to eight minutes, then says `run this again` — with the reason (a session's ten-minute Bash ceiling) and the exit code. Add § *The door* after § *The gate form*: the plan boundary, checked before the gate for a pull request from a project branch, with `unauthorisedChanges` and `stepOfPr` named. `docs/technical/mc-run.md` lines 736–789 (*A hand `mc merge` that was refused becomes the runner's*): rewrite the first paragraph to say `busy` and `lease` no longer queue because the verb waits, and leave the rest for step 3. Add a changelog fragment under `changelog.d/`.

steps.title: The step session lands its own pull request, and the runner lands none of a session's
steps.done_when: `canon/roles/step.md` and `stepPrompt` tell the session to set `done` and `pr`, commit, push, open the pull request and run `mc merge <repo> <pr>` until it is merged, fixing a red in the same session; `runStep` in `src/mc/run.js` calls neither `landProject` nor `landPr` for a step's pull request and writes `success,merged` / `success,open` / `success` from GitHub's state of the branch's pull request; `docs/technical/mc-run.md` § *The session* and § *The merge* say so; the suite is green.
instruction: Read first: `canon/roles/step.md` whole (line 28 is the sentence this step reverses: "Do not merge: the runner lands it after you, and its gate re-runs the test selection on the merged tree"); `stepPrompt` in `src/mc/run-plan.js` lines 762–797 (line 793: `Do not merge. Do not ask questions. Stop when the PR exists.`); `runStep` in `src/mc/run.js` from the session call at line 1971 to the return at 2082 — the `openNow` list (1995–2013), `pr` (2014), the trespass check (2037–2054), the hold (2061–2063), the landing (2065–2070), `logRun` (2072); `landProject` (827–865) and `landPr` (674–733); `landingNote` in run-plan.js; the tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js` that assert a landing after a step (`grep -n "landProject\|mergeRound\|success,merged" tests/mc/run.test.js`). Also `tests/mc/roles.test.js` and `tests/mc/run-plan.test.js` for the prompt's closing lines.

The role. Replace the *Otherwise build it …* paragraph and the *Do not merge* sentence of `canon/roles/step.md` with the sequence, in this order and as a numbered list the session can follow: run what `done_when` names; set your step `done` with its `pr` — you do not have the number yet, so commit the code first, open the pull request from this branch, then write the number into `pr` and commit that as a second commit on the same branch (or open the pull request, read the number, write it, and amend: say which, once); push; run `mc merge <repo> <pr>` in the foreground, and read every line it prints. Then the three answers: `merged #N into main` — the step is done, stop. A red — the lines name every red test and every failed command gate with its output; fix the code (never lower a threshold, delete, skip or weaken a test: the gate decides), commit, push to the same branch, run `mc merge` again on the same pull request. `plan-trespass` — undo the change to whatever is not your step's `status`, `pr`, `comments` or `met`, commit, push, run it again. `still waiting … run this again` — run it again. `conflicts with origin/main` — merge `origin/main` into your branch, keep both intents, push, run it again. Say also what a session does not do: it never runs `gh pr merge`, never opens a second pull request, never edits a step that is not its own, and never sets `done` on a step whose pull request it could not land. And when to stop without landing: the same red three times with nothing new to try, or a red whose fix needs a decision that is not the session's — leave `done` and `pr` as written (the plan on `main` is untouched until the merge), write what the gate said and what was tried into the pull request body and into the step's `comments` in one more commit, and stop; an open pull request on this branch is a person's through the brief. Keep the role's frontmatter and the paragraphs on the plan boundary, the blocked route, the merge-in-progress preamble and the branch rule.

The prompt. In `stepPrompt`, replace line 793 with the same rule in three lines: build it, set `done` and `pr`, open the pull request, then `mc merge <repo> <pr>` until it says merged — a red comes back to you, fix it and run it again; never `gh pr merge`. Put `<repo>` in as the repository's name (`repo` is a parameter) so the command is copyable. The prompt's earlier sentence *The runner compares the file before and after and will leave your PR unmerged if you changed anything else* becomes *`mc merge` compares the plan on main with yours and refuses the pull request if you changed anything else* — that is step 1's door. Update the `stepPrompt` tests in `tests/mc/run-plan.test.js` that match the closing line.

The runner. In `runStep`: remove the landing (`if (merge && openNow.length && note === 'success') { landProject … }`, lines 2065–2070) and the hold written after a session (`holdsAfterSession`, 2061–2063 — step 3 removes `hold` itself; here just stop calling it from this path, and leave `held.json` writes elsewhere untouched so the interim tree still parses). Replace them with one question to GitHub: the state of the pull request on `branch` — `gh pr list --head <branch> --state all --json number,state --limit 1` in the worktree, or `gh pr view <branch> --json number,state`; `MERGED` → `note = 'success,merged'` and `pr` the number; `OPEN` → `'success,open'`; none → `'success'` as today. `landSeconds` is `null` (the column stays, the cell reads `-`). The `openNow` list stays for `pr` and for the *#N is on <branch>, not a branch named after the project* line. The post-session trespass check (2037–2054) stays in this step, because the runner still writes `plan-trespass` into the row and the log for a session that is now refused at `mc merge`'s door — the two say the same thing about the same file; step 3 decides whether the row keeps the word. Return `'merged'` on `success,merged` exactly as before so the lane picks again.

`askForUpdate` (run.js line 761) fires today from `landPr` when a landing touched `src/mc/` or `canon/`. With the session landing, the runner has to ask the same question after the session: call `askForUpdate(repo, name, pr)` when the note is `success,merged`, from `runStep`, with the same `gh pr view --json files` it uses now. Otherwise a step that changed the runner's own code lands and the running runner never hands over — which is the case measured on 2026-09-02 that the function was written for.

`current-<repo>.json` and the page: nothing changes in this step; the session is running for the whole of its own `mc merge`, and the page's MERGES section shows the round from the gate lock as it does for any round. The `starting` line and runs.tsv columns are as they are.

The merge lane in `runLoop` (`mergeQueued`, `runner.mergeQueued()` at line 2437) keeps running in this step over what `queueRefusal` still writes for `red`/`pr-tests`/`extra-gate`/`merge` — a hand `mc merge` that went red is still handed to it and its `laneRepair` still fires. That is step 3's removal; do not touch it here, so that this pull request is the session's behaviour and nothing else.
